en: 2 important terms you must know when talking
about AI and also large language models.
Training versus inference. Training is the
part that happens when a large language
model is created, when that neural network
is created.
Inference then is what happens when that
model is there to serve customers. When
you're using ChatGPT, you are using the
inference part of the
GPT model in the end.
So the GPT model was trained by OpenAI, but
then it's put on their servers once it's
done training,
and there it's running to take your request,
for example, and produce some text output
for you. And that part is called inference.
So when you hear people talk about
inference, what they really just mean is
that the model is running on some server
serving requests like yours coming from
ChatGPT, for example.
It's the inference part where the model and
all its parameters need to
be run on a server. And therefore it's that
part that also requires quite beefy
hardware. Well, actually the training does
too, but different kinds of hardware. For
the inference, you especially need machines
with lots of memory because all these
parameters that were derived during training
need to be loaded into memory so that
incoming requests can be funneled through
them and can produce output. So if you
wanted to run a large language model on your
computer, you would need a lot of memory.
That's why small language models can be
quite attractive because they're using the
same technique but have less parameters and
therefore require less memory.
